qa.question: Can a follower or amulet with a "Q" ability also be played when an enemy follower attacks or during my opponent's end phase?
qa.answer:
No. The "Q" icon is tied to a specific card ability, not the card itself, so the follower or amulet cannot be played as if it had Quick.
An ability with a "Q" icon can be played with the same timing as Quick when in the appropriate zone.

qa.title: Q297 (Sep. 29, 2023)

qa.answer:
The "Q" icon indicates that the ability can be played with Quick timing.
Abilities with this icon, like cards with Quick, can be played like usual during your main phase, as well as when an enemy follower attacks or during your opponent's end phase.

qa.title: Q834 (Aug. 8, 2024)
qa.question: If I have this follower on the field and it has 6 attack. If I attack the enemy leader, and they play Realm of Repose's activated ability with Quick, how much damage does the enemy leader take?
qa.answer:
They take either 4 damage or 5 damage. When there are multiple abilities modifying damage dealt, the player receiving the damage decides the order the abilities are applied. In this case, depending on the order, the final damage taken can be calculated as follows:

The enemy leader takes 4 damage because they decide to apply this follower's ability to increase the damage dealt by 1 first, so this follower will deal 7 damage before Realm of Repose's ability reduces the damage dealt to their leader to 4.

The enemy leader takes 5 damage because they decide to apply Realm of Repose's ability first, so this follower will deal 6 damage before Realm of Repose's ability reduces the damage to their leader to 4. Then, this follower's ability increases the damage dealt by 1 will take effect so this follower will deal 5 damage.

qa.title: Q833 (Aug. 8, 2024)
qa.question: If this follower is on my field, and I attack an enemy Lævateinn Dragon, Defense Form with a 1-attack One-Tailed Fox, how much damage does Lævateinn Dragon, Defense Form take?
qa.answer:
It takes either 0 damage or 1 damage. When there are multiple abilities modifying damage dealt, the player receiving the damage decides the order the abilities are applied. In this case, depending on the order, the final damage taken can be calculated as follows:

Lævateinn Dragon, Defense Form takes 1 damage because its controller decides to apply the follower's ability to increase the damage dealt by 1 first, so the One-Tailed Fox will deal 2 damage before Lævateinn Dragon, Defense Form's ability reduces the damage dealt by 1.

Lævateinn Dragon, Defense Form takes 0 damage because its controller decides to apply Lævateinn Dragon, Defense Form's ability to reduce damage dealt by 1 first, so the One-Tailed Fox will deal 0 damage before this follower's ability increases the damage dealt by 1. However, this follower's "if a Yokai follower on your field would deal damage, it deals that much plus 1 instead" only takes effect when damage is dealt, and 0 damage does not count as dealing damage. So, the ability does not take effect and the damage taken by Lævateinn Dragon, Defense Form remains 0.

qa.answer:
It takes 3 damage. When there are multiple abilities modifying damage dealt, the player receiving the damage decides the order the abilities are applied.

In this case, whether this follower's ability increases the damage dealt by 1 first, or Lævateinn Dragon, Defense Form's ability reduces damage dealt by 1 first, the damage taken is 3.

qa.title: Q743 (Jun. 14, 2024)
qa.question: When my opponent has a Lyrial, Archer Throne with 5 or less defense on their field, why does playing Dance of Death not deal damage to the enemy leader, while playing Fiery Embrace with Spellchain (10) does?
qa.answer:
It has to do with the timing at which the enemy Lyrial is destroyed, or in other words, the duration for which its ability remains valid.

First, let's look at Dance of Death. When a follower's defense becomes 0 or less, it gets destroyed at the next Confirmation Timing, which occurs after the current ability—Dance of Death, in this case—is resolved. Therefore, when Dance of Death deals 2 damage to the enemy leader, Lyrial has 0 or less defense, but it's still on your opponent's field, so its ability is still valid, preventing its leader from taking ability damage.

Now let's look at Fiery Embrace with Spellchain (10). Effects indicated by an ability are applied in the written order, so the instruction "destroy it (the enemy follower)" is executed first, and Lyrial is immediately destroyed. By the time the instruction "deal 3 damage to that follower's leader" is executed, Lyrial is no longer on the field, so its ability isn't valid, and the enemy leader can take ability damage.

qa.title: Q742 (Jun. 14, 2024)

qa.answer: No, and no. Sanguine only becomes active for you if your leader loses defense during your turn.

qa.answer: No. Humpty Dumpty's On Evolve ability deals 5 damage to Lyrial, bringing its defense to 0 or less, but it's not destroyed until Humpty Dumpty's ability is fully resolved, so Lyrial's ability is still valid when you would've dealt 3 damage to its leader.

qa.title: Q735 (Jun. 14, 2024)

qa.answer: Ability damage is all damage except for damage dealt by two followers in combat or by a follower attacking a leader. For example, damage from an evolved Izudia, Omen of Unkilling's activated ability, "Deal 6 damage to each enemy leader with at least 10 defense," counts as ability damage.

qa.title: Q344 (Dec. 8, 2023)
qa.question: When an ability refers to the cost of a card that was played for a different number of play points than its displayed cost, does it refer to that different number?
qa.answer:
No. It refers to the cost displayed on the card. For example, when referring to the cost of a Flame Destroyer, the number used is always 9, even if it was played for 6, 3, or 0 play points.

Effects that change the number of play points it costs to play a card don't change the cost information of the card. When an ability refers to how much a card "costs" or its "base cost," it always refers to the cost displayed on the card. Note that, when referring to the cost of an evolved follower, you use the cost of its unevolved form.
